purpose: Check the standard Taylor and implicit-differentiation background; this is not a literature novelty search or evidence for the source-specific coefficients.

sources.title: Math 51H – Mean value theorem, Taylor’s theorem and integrals
sources.author: Mathematics Department, Stanford University; individual author not stated in the retrieved text
sources.actual_read_scope: Retrieved full PDF text, four pages; applied passage pp.2–3, second-order formula (3) and continuity-of-Hessian remainder argument.
sources.relation: supports standard mathematical method; contextual for the physical one-sided construction
sources.supports: A continuous Hessian gives a second-order Taylor polynomial with a Peano remainder along allowed line segments.
sources.limits: The displayed standard theorem assumes an open domain. The PHYS29 physical half-domain root argument and support-preserving endpoint paths are separately derived. No numerical remainder bound comes from this source. Higher-order formula transcription contains a repeated-argument typo; that formula is not used.

sources.title: 18.022: Multivariable calculus — The implicit function theorem
sources.author: MIT Mathematics course handout, hosted under Lars Hesselholt’s course path; individual byline not displayed in retrieved document
sources.publication_date: not stated in PDF; hosting path labels F2007
sources.actual_read_scope: Retrieved full two-page PDF text: theorem on p.1, differentiated constraint and inverse-Jacobian formula on p.2.
sources.relation: supports standard first implicit derivative; contextual only for second-order and one-sided extensions
sources.supports: A nonzero scalar derivative in the solved variable supplies the local simple-root condition and the first implicit derivative on an open domain.
sources.limits: This C1 handout does not itself prove PHYS29’s one-sided C2 root formula, source model, threshold existence, or numerical values. Those require the direct derivation and inherited premises.
